Operator:
Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the StellarTech Second Quarter Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a Q&A session. Today's call is being recorded.
I would now like to hand the call over to Janet Davies, Investor Relations Director. Please go ahead.

Janet Davies, Investor Relations Director:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and welcome to StellarTech’s earnings call. Joining me today are Robert Thompson, CEO; Susan Miller, CFO; and David Lee, Chief Technology Officer.
Earlier today, we published our earnings press release and slides, which are available on our IR site. Please note this call may contain forward-looking statements. Now, I’ll turn it over to Robert Thompson.

Robert Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Janet. Hello, everyone.

Let’s start with a look at the quarter:

We made strong progress this quarter. Our Diluted EPS for Q2 reached $2.57, and our Return on Equity stood at 16.2%. This Diluted EPS reflects a 12% increase compared to Q2 of the previous fiscal year, where our Diluted EPS was $2.29. This growth is attributable to a 9% increase in overall revenue, climbing from $1.9 billion to $2.07 billion. We also saw great momentum in our HPC sector, generating $1.44 billion in revenue, accounting for 32% of our total Q2 revenue. This represents a substantial 23% QoQ increase from $1.17 billion in Q1 2024, making it the fastest-growing segment this quarter.

These achievements underscore our commitment to disciplined execution and innovation.

Now I’ll pass it to Susan Miller to walk through in more detail.

Susan Miller, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Robert, and hello, everyone.

Let me take you through the financials:

First, building on what Robert said, we’ve continued to drive improvements in the HPC segment, driven by surging demand for AI and machine learning applications. We are witnessing significant traction in the cloud computing, data analytics, and scientific research sectors. Our latest generation of GPUs, featuring enhanced parallel processing capabilities, are resonating strongly with customers seeking to accelerate their AI workloads. We are actively expanding our partnerships with leading cloud service providers and research institutions to further penetrate this rapidly growing market.

We invested strategically in capital expenditures. During our Q1 call, we guided to a full-year CapEx budget in the range of $10 billion to $11 billion. This budget was predicated on our then-current assessment of market demand, planned technological upgrades, and anticipated capacity expansions. However, over the last three months, we've witnessed a significant acceleration in the global deployment of 5G infrastructure and the proliferation of 5G-enabled devices, particularly in China, South Korea, and parts of Europe. We now anticipate that our full-year 2019 CapEx will likely exceed the high end of our previously guided range. Our preliminary assessment suggests a potential increase of approximately 10% to 15% above the high end of our original guidance. This would translate to a revised CapEx budget of between $11 billion and $12.65 billion for the full year.

Additionally, we’ve seen progress in gross margins, and we believe this will continue. Our second-quarter gross margin reached 43%, representing a 1.7 percentage point improvement compared to the 41.3% reported in the first quarter. This increase can be primarily attributed to the resolution of the photoresist defect material incident that impacted Q1 and a more favorable foreign exchange rate environment. However, compared to Q2 2018, when our gross margin stood at 45.5%, we see a 2.5 percentage point decline, primarily driven by N7 ramp-up costs and a shift in product mix.

Now I’ll turn it over to David, who will speak about operations and innovation.

David Lee, Chief Technology Officer:
Thanks, Susan.

Let me begin with a closer look at the Net Margin and Diluted EPS results, particularly on the revenue growth front. We experienced a solid 9% increase in overall revenue, climbing from $1.9 billion in Q2 of the previous FY to $2.07 billion this quarter. This growth was particularly strong in our North American market, driven by the successful launch of our new "Synergy" product line. However, our European market saw slightly slower growth at 6%, reflecting ongoing economic uncertainties in the region. We introduced Synergy, and it’s already contributing to enhanced performance.

I’d also like to expand on our sales guidance. We anticipate continued growth across all platforms in Q3, with smartphones and High-Performance Computing (HPC) leading the charge. We project a strong Q3 for our smartphone platform, driven by the successful launch of our Gen-Z series chipset and increased market share in emerging markets. We anticipate a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion. HPC continues to be a strong performer, and we project a 12% increase in revenue year-over-year to $1.8 billion, primarily driven by demand for AI and machine learning applications.

Let’s move to the Q&A.

Q&A SESSION

Analyst 1:
You mentioned strong improvements in the HPC sector. Can you talk more about the specific initiatives driving this growth?

Susan Miller:
Certainly. Our HPC segment boasts the highest gross margin at 52%, a slight improvement from 51% in Q1, driven by economies of scale and optimized production processes. We are investing heavily in next-generation chip architectures and advanced packaging technologies to maintain our leadership in the HPC space. This includes exploring chiplet designs and 3D stacking to enhance performance and reduce power consumption. We are also working closely with software developers to optimize AI frameworks and libraries for our hardware, creating a seamless and efficient development experience. The recent partnership with Oak Ridge National Laboratory is a testament to our commitment to pushing the boundaries of HPC innovation.

Analyst 2:
Can you elaborate on the trajectory of the automotive segment and the impact of supply chain disruptions?

David Lee:
Sure. The Automotive segment generated $225 Million in revenue, accounting for 5% of total Q2 revenue. This represents a modest 3% QoQ increase from $218 Million in Q1 2024, reflecting the ongoing challenges in the automotive industry, including supply chain disruptions and chip shortages. We are working closely with automotive manufacturers to develop customized solutions for their specific needs. This includes collaborating on the design and development of autonomous driving platforms and electric vehicle powertrains. We are also investing in automotive-grade components and manufacturing processes to ensure the highest levels of reliability and safety. Specifically, our work with Tesla on the next-generation full self-driving (FSD) chip is expected to be a major catalyst for growth in the coming years. For the full year, we anticipate a challenging year for the automotive segment, projecting a decline of 8% year-over-year, resulting in approximately $1.6 billion in revenue, due to ongoing supply chain disruptions, the EV transition, and geopolitical risks.

Analyst 3:
With regard to gross margins, how does the cost improvement initiative at the N7 node impact your outlook?

Susan Miller:
Our engineering teams are actively focused on optimizing process parameters, improving yield rates, and negotiating more favorable material pricing for the N7 node. For the third quarter of 2019, we are guiding for a gross margin improvement of approximately 4 percentage points sequentially at the midpoint. This improvement is primarily predicated on the expectation of a higher level of overall capacity utilization across our manufacturing facilities. We expect the cost improvement initiatives at the N7 node to gain traction in Q3, contributing to the gross margin expansion. Assuming we can maintain high capacity utilization rates, which we believe is achievable given the robust demand environment, we remain confident in our ability to achieve a gross margin target of approximately 50% in the medium to long term. This target is contingent on continued progress in advanced node technology, efficient capacity management, and successful cost optimization efforts.

Closing

Robert Thompson:
Thank you all for joining us today. We're energized by the momentum we’re seeing and look forward to sharing continued progress next quarter.

Operator:
Thank you. This concludes the call. You may now disconnect.
